samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the mount effect's deps makes the editor/store rebuild reachable, but the cleanup never releases `YorkieDocStore`'s `doc.subscribe`, so a stale store keeps driving a disposed editor
samples.evidence: The effect body builds a fresh store per run (`docs-view.tsx:356 const store = new YorkieDocStore(doc)`), and `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor subscribes to the Yorkie doc and DISCARDS the unsubscribe handle: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:622 doc.subscribe((event) => { … this.onRemoteChange?.(); })`. The class exposes no `dispose()`/`unsubscribe` (grep found none), and the effect cleanup at `docs-view.tsx:549-571` only calls `editor.dispose()` and nulls the refs. Before this change the effect ran once per `doc`, so the leak was tied to a doc swap; with `readOnly` in the deps a share link re-resolving from `editor` to `viewer` (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:322 const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, fed from a react-query result that can refetch) re-runs it. Afterwards every `remote-change` still fires the OLD store's callback, which calls `editor.clearImageSelection()` / `editor.getDoc().refresh()` / `editor.render()` on the disposed editor (`docs-view.tsx:410-439`) and `store.publishResolvedLocalCursor(...)` on the stale store — a second presence writer for the same doc, painting into the canvas removed by `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4412 canvas.remove()`. Fix belongs on the new code: give `YorkieDocStore` an unsubscribe and call it in this cleanup.

samples.summary: The three sibling Yorkie stores still gate undo on a recorded stack DEPTH and their comments point at `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`, a field this change removed — the same 50-entry-cap bug remains there

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.replaceDocument()`/`setDocument()` now clear the redo stack, diverging from `YorkieDocStore` (whose `replaceDocument` is a no-op) and from the `DocStore` interface doc
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:16-21` documents `replaceDocument` only as "Replace the internal document WITHOUT pushing to the undo stack" and says nothing about redo; `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:863-864` implements it as a no-op, so under the collaborative store redo survives a `replaceDocument()` while under `MemDocStore` (`memory.ts:62-65`, now `willWrite()`) it does not. The only live caller today is a test (`packages/docs/test/model/document.test.ts:1085`), so nothing breaks now, but the two stores answer differently for an interface member whose contract the diff otherwise works hard to keep identical.

samples.summary: The host's throttled cursor publisher now runs inside an open batch for typing/paste/Enter and is silently dropped, so peer caret updates depend entirely on each mutator's own history-presence write
samples.evidence: `docs-view.tsx:452-469` publishes the local caret from `editor.onCursorMove(...)` via `store.updateCursorPos(pos, sel)`. `cursor.moveTo(...)` now happens INSIDE `withUndoUnit` (e.g. `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1029-1039`, `:2661`, `:1552`), and `YorkieDocStore.updateCursorPos` early-returns while a batch is open (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:3217` → `skipNonHistoryPresence()` at `:3242`). The immediate (unthrottled) publish is therefore dropped with no trailing timer scheduled; peers only see whatever the last store write's `recordHistoryPresence` recorded (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:3107`), which for actions ending in a style/auto-link write is not necessarily the final caret. Would need a two-client check to confirm a visible stale caret.

samples.summary: Two render entry points bypass the new render-hold wrapper and would paint mid-batch if ever reached from inside an undo unit
samples.evidence: The hold is implemented only in the `requestRender` closure (`text-editor.ts:734-743`); `text-editor.ts:2268 (this.requestRenderNoCursorScroll ?? this.requestRender)()` and `text-editor.ts:2981 (this.requestCursorRender ?? this.requestRender)()` call the host variants (`editor.ts:2522` / `editor.ts:2525` → `render` / `renderCursorMove`) directly, so they paint immediately regardless of `undoUnitDepth`. Today their callers (table resize drag, caret navigation) run outside any unit, so nothing is broken now — but the invariant "no paint inside a unit" is enforced at one of three seams, and a future mutation path reaching either one escapes it silently.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor subscribes to the Yorkie doc and discards the unsubscribe handle (yorkie-doc-store.ts:612-628), and a grep for `dispose|unsubscribe|unsub` in that file returns no matches — the class has no teardown. The mount effect constructs a new store per run (docs-view.tsx:356) and installs `store.onRemoteChange` (docs-view.tsx:410-439), while the cleanup (docs-view.tsx:549-571) only calls `unsubPresence()`, `editor.dispose()` and nulls the refs; it never releases the store subscription nor clears `onRemoteChange` (that property is assigned only at :410). Since `readOnly` is now in the deps (docs-view.tsx:581), a re-run leaves the previous store live, invoking `editor.clearImageSelection()/getDoc().refresh()/render()` on an editor whose canvas was removed by `dispose()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4382-4412) and writing presence from a stale store. No guard elsewhere neutralises the retained callback. The only inaccuracy in the reviewer's account is the reachability mechanism — `readOnly` comes from a one-shot `useState`+`resolveShareLink` fetch (shared-document.tsx:1082-1102, :322, :364), not a refetching react-query, so a role flip with a stable `docKey` (shared-document.tsx:984-993) requires a `token` prop change to a different token on the same document; that lowers likelihood but does not make the path provably unreachable, and the same stale-store leak also exists on the `doc`-swap re-run. This is an invariant ("one store per doc, never torn down") violated in a file the diff does not show, i.e. in the blast-radius lane, with major impact.

finding.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the mount-effect deps makes the effect re-runnable, but the cleanup never disposes `YorkieDocStore` — the old store stays subscribed to the Yorkie doc and drives the DISPOSED editor (and publishes presence) on every remote change.
finding.evidence: `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor registers `doc.subscribe(...)` and discards the unsubscribe (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:622); the class has no `dispose()`/`unsubscribe` at all (grep over that file returns no matches). The effect cleanup (docs-view.tsx:549-571) unsubscribes presence and calls `editor.dispose()`, but only sets `storeRef.current = null` — it never clears `store.onRemoteChange` (installed at docs-view.tsx:410) nor tears down the store's own doc subscription. Before this delta the effect keyed on `[didMount, doc]` and effectively ran once per document, so the leak was unobservable. Now every `readOnly` transition builds a second `YorkieDocStore` while the first one lives on: on the next remote change the stale handler runs `editor.clearImageSelection()`, `editor.getDoc().refresh()`, `editor.restoreLocalCursor(...)`, `editor.render()` against the disposed editor (whose canvas was removed and whose measure caches were released at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4405-4412), and then `store.publishResolvedLocalCursor(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1274-1286) writes presence through the RAW, un-read-only store — clobbering the live editor's caret broadcast with the stale one, from a session that may have just lost write authority. Fix belongs in the new code path: clear `store.onRemoteChange` and unsubscribe the store in the cleanup (or give `YorkieDocStore` a `dispose()`).

verdict.reason: All claimed facts check out. docs-view.tsx:581 now keys the mount effect on `readOnly`, making it re-runnable; docs-view.tsx:356 builds a fresh `YorkieDocStore` each run, and yorkie-doc-store.ts:612-628 registers `doc.subscribe(...)` in the constructor while discarding the unsubscribe, with no `dispose()`/`unsubscribe` anywhere in the class. The cleanup at docs-view.tsx:549-571 only calls `unsubPresence()`, `editor.dispose()` and nulls the refs — it never clears `store.onRemoteChange` (installed at docs-view.tsx:410) nor tears down the store's doc subscription. The stale handler captures `editor`/`store` lexically (not via `editorRef.current`), so on the next remote change it drives the disposed editor (`editor.dispose()` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4382-4413 removes the canvas, disposes the measure cache, disconnects the observer, and sets no `disposed` guard) and then writes presence via `store.publishResolvedLocalCursor` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1274-1286) through the raw, non-read-only store. A `readOnly` flip while mounted is reachable: shared-document.tsx:322 derives it from `resolved.role` and passes it at :364, which is the very scenario the new comment cites. In lane as a lifecycle/ownership invariant that YorkieDocStore and EditorAPI.dispose (both outside the diff) rely on; major severity fits.
